title: Multi-Query attention kernel arbiter + memory-safety tuning
creator: Asha Patel
description: We are seeing intermittent OOMs and degraded latency P95 for short-sequence multi-query (MQ) workloads after integrating FlashAttention v3 kernels in the runtime. Investigation points to two correlated issues: (1) the MQ memory workspace estimators in the kernel selector over-allocate for certain batch/shard shapes on compute capability 8.x, and (2) prefill->decode scheduling currently favors maximum batching which conflicts with MQ’s lowered per-head state and ends up thrashing GPU memory on mixed-length batches. This ticket implements a kernel arbiter that chooses between v2/v3 Flash kernels and matmul-based fallback at request-time, adds conservative workspace safety margins, and introduces prefill/decode scheduling hints for MQ workloads. Goal: eliminate OOMs, restore P95 latency SLOs for interactive MQ customers, and provide telemetry to tune heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: No OOMs observed in perf cluster for MQ test-suite over 72h
P95 latency for MQ interactive workload within 1.2x baseline (pre-integration) on A100 and H100
Kernel arbiter exposes flags to force v2/v3/matmul for canary rollouts
All changes covered by unit + integration tests in perf CI
Operational telemetry added: kernel_choice, workspace_requested, workspace_granted, fallback_reason
tasks: Design kernel arbiter API in runtime (config + dynamic heuristic)
Implement conservative workspace estimator for MQ in selector
Add scheduling hints and 'prefer-small-batches' option for prefill path
Integrate arbiter into prefill/decode code paths and expose runtime flags
Create perf CI job to run MQ mixed-length suite across A100/H100
Write unit tests for estimator edge-cases and memory accounting
Run 72h soak on perf cluster and analyze telemetry
Prepare canary rollout plan and rollback criteria
reproduction_steps: Deploy to perf-GPU pool (A100-40G) with MQ stress harness enabled
Run mixed-length workload: batch sizes [1,4,8], seq lengths [64,128,512], head_dim 64, num_heads 16
Observe OOMs in /var/log/runtime/oom.log and kernel_choice metrics in telemetry
Replay failing traces with per-request shape logging to reproduce workspace over-allocation
benchmarks: Baseline (pre-Flash v3): GPT-like MQ seq=128 batch=8 A100 throughput=420 tok/s, P95=42ms
After v3 (no arbiter): MQ seq=128 batch=8 A100 throughput=460 tok/s, P95=68ms (regression) with OOMs in mixed-batches
Arbiter + conservative estimator (dev): MQ seq=128 batch=8 A100 throughput=435 tok/s, P95=45ms, no OOMs in 24h run
experiments: Vary workspace margin pct: [0%, 10%, 25%] — 10% best tradeoff between perf and safety
Scheduling hint 'prefer-small-batches' enabled/disabled — mitigates decode thrash for mixed-length inputs
Force v2/v3/matmul per-request to measure perf envelope and failure modes
Test across CC61 (A100) and CC89 (H100) — H100 needs larger workspace margin for some v3 kernels
decisions: Introduce kernel arbiter at runtime edge: choose kernel by tuple (device_cc, seq_len, batch, head_dim, quant_mode)
Default policy: prefer Flash v3 for long sequences (>256) on H100/A100, prefer v2 or matmul for short sequences or when workspace > 70% GPU free
Conservative workspace margin: +10% by default, configurable per-customer
Add telemetry fields to understand fallback frequency before removing conservative margin
